keyVerseText: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מִשְׁעֵן (mishʻên) derives from the root שָׁעַן (shâʻan), which means to lean, rely, or rest upon. This root conveys the fundamental idea of support or dependence, emphasizing a physical or figurative act of leaning on something for stability. Unlike the English word "stay," which can mean to remain in place, the root sense highlights an active reliance or trust, suggesting a source of strength or sustenance that one can lean upon.
usageInScripture: The word מִשְׁעֵן appears five times in Scripture, consistently translated as "stay" or "was my stay." This demonstrates a stable semantic range centered on the concept of support or a sustaining presence. The frequent use of "stay" reflects both a literal and figurative support, whether as a physical staff or as a protector and sustainer. The consistency in translation underscores the word's role in expressing dependable strength or refuge.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מִשְׁעֵן in its original sense enriches our grasp of God as a reliable support and protector. The imagery of leaning or resting upon God conveys a deep trust and dependence that is foundational to faith. This word reminds believers that God is not a distant or impersonal force but a sustaining presence who upholds us in times of trouble. Recognizing God as our מִשְׁעֵן encourages a posture of reliance and confidence in His providential care, which is central to the Christian life and witness.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 22:19, the psalmist declares, "They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay." Here, מִשְׁעֵן conveys more than mere presence; it portrays God as the firm support and refuge amid adversity. The term enriches the verse by emphasizing that God is the one on whom the psalmist can lean when overwhelmed, highlighting divine faithfulness and strength in times of distress.
